candidate.title: Drop-Seq
candidate.scope: The lower, explicitly labeled Drop-Seq row of the assigned Illumina single-cell poster crop: droplet co-compartmentalization, bead capture of polyadenylated mRNA, bead pooling, cDNA synthesis/amplification and sequencing. The upper CytoSeq row is a separately labeled neighboring poster workflow, not an alternative branch of this Drop-Seq card. The partial chemical legend at the right has no route into this row. The scope is schematic architecture, clarified by the Macosko Drop-Seq implementation, not a complete execution protocol.

states.label: Microparticles bearing barcoded oligonucleotide primers
features: Bead-attached DNA oligos contain Universal, Cell label, Molecular index and terminal Oligo(dT) segments as labeled in the drawing.
The primary implementation identifies these as a constant PCR/sequencing priming sequence, a barcode shared by primers on a bead, a UMI varying among primers, and oligo-dT for poly(A) capture.
Primers are synthesized on the bead from 5′ to 3′, leaving free 3′ ends available for capture-associated priming; no other end chemistry is inferred from the generic icon.

states.label: Sequence readout of barcoded cDNA representing single-cell mRNA
features: The drawing calls the endpoint Barcoded mRNA from single cells; this denotes the represented RNA target.

Transcript sequence identifies the expressed gene; the cell barcode assigns the captured transcript to a bead-associated cell compartment, and the UMI distinguishes captured molecules from PCR duplicates.
In the primary implementation, one paired read supplies the cell barcode and UMI, and its mate supplies transcript-derived cDNA sequence for gene assignment.
These are measurements of captured polyadenylated transcripts, rather than an exhaustive census of all cellular RNA or full-length transcript structures.
A bead barcode indicates a captured compartment: cell doublets and ambient RNA can compromise single-cell attribution, and capture is incomplete.
